mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a consistent week-on-week narrowing of its deficit from -44.4 to -37.6 over the last four weeks. This autoregressive momentum in retail footfall recovery is expected to persist, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved monotonically from -44.4 to -37.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days despite four consecutive weeks of prior improvement.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility crosses a weekly improvement threshold of more than 1.5 points, it signals renewed willingness to travel for non-essential purposes, which feeds into retail visits within two weeks as commuters and shoppers resume transit-based trips to shopping districts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 1.5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -74.1 to -73.0, a 1.1 point improvement in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean does not rise over the subsequent two weeks despite TRANSIT crossing the 1.5-point weekly improvement threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A joint decline in RESIDENTIAL time-at-home combined with rising WORKPLACES mobility indicates coordinated relaxation of stay-at-home policy, which together amplify retail visitation beyond what either series would predict alone, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 20.1 to 18.0 while WORKPLACES improved from -36.0 to -33.0 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks even when RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES simultaneously rises in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: During a reopening regime, a sharp rise in PARKS mobility reflects increased outdoor leisure activity that typically precedes a spillover into nearby retail and recreation venues as households combine outdoor trips with shopping errands, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose sharply from -39.4 to -25.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks despite PARKS mobility continuing its upward trajectory.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility narrows past a -1.5 threshold, it indicates near-normalization of essential shopping trips, which is a short-horizon leading indicator that broader retail activity will also normalize upward within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -2.4 to -1.0 in the latest week, crossing -1.5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean does not rise in the immediate following week after GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -1.5.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility signals a compound return to pre-pandemic commuting and work patterns; the interaction of these two series captures a structural shift in daily routines that drives sustained retail footfall growth over four weeks, exceeding what either series predicts independently.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved in the latest week (-74.1 to -73.0 and -35.1 to -33.0 respectively)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over four weeks even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show concurrent weekly improvement.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, any uptick in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals renewed compliance with stay-at-home policy, which would suppress retail visitation over the following two weeks as households reduce discretionary outings.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week by more than 0.5 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 19.3 to 20.1 between t-3w and t-2w before declining again
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks despite a RESIDENTIAL uptick exceeding 0.5 points, indicating the policy-compliance mechanism is inactive.

mechanism_narrative: Outdoor parks usage, as a proxy for favorable weather and daylight conditions, exhibits a steady upward trend that drives short-term increases in nearby retail and recreation visits within a one-week lag as people combine outdoor activity with shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved every week from -39.4 to -25.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week immediately following a week of PARKS improvement.
